title: The Leftmost Value in the Last Row

concept.title: Walk the levels from right to left, the last node is the answer
body: We want the leftmost value of the deepest level. A level-order walk that adds the **right child before the left child** visits every level from right to left, and the very last node it visits is the leftmost node of the deepest level. So the answer is simply "the last node taken from the queue".
Another way is a depth-first walk that remembers the depth: the first node found on a new deepest level (when going left before right) is the answer. Both versions need only one pass over the tree.

statement: Print the value of the leftmost node on the deepest level (the last row) of a binary tree.
inputFormat: The first line has `t`, the number of words in the description of the tree.
The second line has the tree in level order: the root first, then the children of the nodes row by row from left to right. `N` stands for a missing child. There is no `N` at the end.
constraints: The height of the tree is at most 800.

examples.note: The last row has the nodes 4, 5 and 6; the leftmost is 4.

hints: The deepest level is the last one in a level-order walk.
Visit the right child before the left child; then the last visited node is the leftmost node of the last row.
Or remember the depth and take the first node of the deepest level in a left-first walk.

import sys
input = sys.stdin.readline

class TreeNode:
    def __init__(self, val, left=None, right=None):
        self.val = val
        self.left = left
        self.right = right


# Builds a binary tree from a level-order list of words; "N" marks a missing child.
def build_tree(vals):
    if not vals or vals[0] == "N":
        return None
    root = TreeNode(int(vals[0]))
    queue = [root]
    head = 0
    i = 1
    while head < len(queue) and i < len(vals):
        node = queue[head]
        head += 1
        if vals[i] != "N":
            node.left = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.left)
        i += 1
        if i < len(vals) and vals[i] != "N":
            node.right = TreeNode(int(vals[i]))
            queue.append(node.right)
        i += 1
    return root

    if root is None:

explanation: A queue walk that enqueues the right child before the left child ends with the leftmost node of the deepest level; that last visited node is the answer.

from collections import deque

def bottom_left(root):
    queue = deque([root])
    node = root
    while queue:
        node = queue.popleft()
        if node.right:
            queue.append(node.right)
        if node.left:
            queue.append(node.left)
    return node.val

t = int(input())
vals = input().split()

print(bottom_left(build_tree(vals)))
